about: Every key of the 22 vendor Tamil keyboards (C:/Shree-Lipi nxt/*.TAM, loaded from their original paths) answered by S8TamU64.dll (TutorGetMappedCodeW, Unicode) and S8Tam764.dll (TutorGetMappedCode, Shree-Lipi 7 raw bytes; the 4/5/6 fonts SHREE-TAM-* draw the same bytes except 9B 9F BA, redrawn ரி ரீ ர்: fonts/family-check.json). Two capture runs (capvo/, capvo-b/) were byte-identical, and each run asked every key twice (#stable 1); every load verified in SLNXT's shared table (#loaded 1). layer 0 = printed keyboard (normal and shift are different ASCII keys), layer 1 = Ctrl+Space, layer 2 = the composer raw code layer (key char = internal code; layers 3..12 answer exactly as layer 2: layers/DOE.tsv; NOT the Ctrl+Shift+1 symbol layer, which the tutor does not expose - see ctrlShift1). Per key: codes = the internal codes the key holds (a conjunct slot expanded, typed order; on INSCRIPT/NEWROMA/PHONET86 the composer ignores the file slots B0-B2 and types its own ோ ொ ௌ), uHex/u = the Unicode composer answer raw / without its carrier, uRead = u in NFC, b7 = the 7 composer bytes. u null = no answer or a placeholder. Carriers to know: a lone pre-base sign (ெ ே ை) comes back on a . carrier from the Unicode composer and as the bare sign glyph F6/F7/F8/F9 from the 7 composer; a lone post-base sign ி ீ ் 5F 40 has no 7 answer (garbage unit count).

ctrlShift1.source: the vendor charts (CHM Special Keys: assets/config/layouts/tam-*.json and tamil-inscript.json symbols; 22 keys in 19 charts, the same minus * in ENG/IE/INDOWORD/one more) + the composers' answers for the internal code of each character (single-code probes, capp/P-results.json). b7 null = the 7 composer types nothing for that code; u null = the Unicode composer has no answer. Bytes under 20 have no glyph in any Tamil face.
